at353_is_closed.detector: walk every text node; a node is a leak when its text contains the credential VERBATIM (the AT-353 shape: the parser has deleted the NULs)
at353_is_closed.positive_control: planted ctlplain (plain credential) and ctlnul (NUL-spelled) DIRECTLY into project.json, bypassing the guard
at353_is_closed.with_controls_planted: both detected; domLength 21 for BOTH, verbatimInDom true for both, textWidth 172px identical -- the NULs are deleted by the parser exactly as cycle 2 measured
at353_is_closed.conclusion: the detector demonstrably fires, and its negative on the guard-accepted set is real

kept_attacking_onboard.method: interleave one code point between every character of the live credential, POST /onboard, then measure what Chromium draws
kept_attacking_onboard.exhaustive_fold_enumeration: enumerate.py walked all 0x110000 code points: 1107659 defeat the fold when interleaved (Cn 826065, Co 137468, Lo 127329, So 6605, Mn 1687, ...). The deny-list covers ~4200 of them.
kept_attacking_onboard.lone_surrogates: not reachable through the HTTP form: urlencoded bodies are utf-8 decoded and a lone surrogate cannot be encoded. Recorded as not-reproducible rather than as a finding.

rendering_measurements.method: per-character Range.getBoundingClientRect; glyphs sorted by screen x give the VISUAL reading order, which is what a human takes off the page

U+202E RLO + reversed.note: pixel-for-pixel the plain-credential control; NO decoding step by the reader

U+2800 braille.visual: visibly spaced Z E B R A ...

the_finding.claim: U+202E RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE plus the reversed credential is accepted by BOTH doors and renders as the exact credential in plain type
the_finding.onboard: HTTP 200, project.json written, home index renders ZEBRA_QUILT_APIKEY_31 (21 glyphs, visual order)
the_finding.case_form: HTTP 200 on title, step_value and step_expected; git-tracked cases.jsonl carries 7 \u202e escapes; the cases page renders the credential in plain type in the title boxes
the_finding.why_the_guard_cannot_see_it: fold_credential(U+202E + reversed) == fold_credential(reversed) -- _is_ignorable strips U+202E as Cf, so the guard DELETES the one character that makes the text render as the credential, then compares a string that is not one
the_finding.why_it_is_not_AT-352: AT-352's filed rationale is that each of its spellings needs a decode step the reader must take. Measured, this one needs none: the browser performs the reordering and prints plain type. That is verbatim the standard on which AT-353 was charged.

false_positives.note: each probe was given a UNIQUE step target so AT-060's duplicate-content 400 could never be mistaken for a credential refusal. A first pass that reused one target DID produce 400s, whose body was the duplicate-case message, not the guard's.
